items.question: What is the minimum flight crew and maximum number of occupants for the H135 T3, per Sect. 2.4?
options: One pilot from the right seat; max 8 persons including flight crew
One pilot from either seat; max 6 persons including flight crew
Two pilots required; max 8 persons including flight crew
One pilot from the left seat; max 9 persons including flight crew
items.explanation: Sect. 2.4 states the minimum flight crew consists of one pilot operating the helicopter from the right crew seat, and the maximum number of occupants comprises up to 8 persons including flight crew.

items.question: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a prohibited flight maneuver in Sect. 2.5.1?
options: Intentional full autorotation landings for training
Hover turns at maximum gross mass
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.1 prohibits aerobatic maneuvers, intentional full autorotation landings for training, and flight into known icing conditions.

items.question: What is the maximum windspeed authorized for rotor starting and stopping, and what is the maximum rear wind component?
options: Max 50 kt from all directions, max 25 kt rear wind component
Max 40 kt from all directions, max 20 kt rear wind component
Max 60 kt from all directions, max 30 kt rear wind component
Max 50 kt only from forward directions, no rear wind permitted
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.2 authorizes rotor starting and stopping for windspeed up to max. 50 kt from all horizontal directions with a maximum rear wind component of 25 kt.

items.question: During slope operations (T/O and landing) greater than 3°, what must be done with the A.TRIM mode?
options: It has no effect on slope operations
It must be set to backup SAS mode
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.4 requires that during slope operations greater than 3°, the A.TRIM mode must be switched off, and cautions not to exceed the allowable mast moment limits.

items.question: What are the maximum slope angles for ground sloping down to the left/right and nose up, per Sect. 2.5.4?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.4 gives max. 14° for ground sloping down to the left or right, max. 12° nose up, and max. 8° nose down (if tail clearance allows).

items.question: In case of mast moment indication failure, what is the maximum permitted slope angle?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.4 states that in case of mast moment indication failure, maximum slope is 6°, referring to the procedure in Sect. 3, Para. 3.3.6.4.

items.question: What is the maximum hover turn rate at gross mass up to 2850 kg, versus above 2850 kg or with HIGH NR mode activated?
options: Max 60°/s up to 2850 kg; max 30°/s above 2850 kg or HIGH NR active, aggressive pedal turns forbidden
Max 30°/s up to 2850 kg; max 60°/s above 2850 kg
Max 60°/s regardless of gross mass, no restriction above 2850 kg
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.5 gives max. 60°/s (6 s for a 360° turn) up to 2850 kg, and max. 30°/s (12 s for a 360° turn) above 2850 kg or with HIGH NR mode activated, where aggressive pedal turns are forbidden.

items.question: What must be selected during any flight with gross mass at or above 2850 kg?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.6 requires that during any flight with GM ≥ 2850 kg, the HIGH NR mode must be selected.

items.question: What is the correct definition of "attentive hands-off" per Sect. 2.6.1?
options: The pilot shall remain attentive to the flight path, but may take hands and feet off the flight controls, and remain ready to take control if required
The pilot must actively control the aircraft with hands and feet on the controls at all times
The pilot shall guard the flight controls without interfering with the AFCS
The pilot may monitor the flight path without any readiness requirement
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.1 defines "attentive hands-off" as: the pilot shall remain attentive to the flight path, but may take hands and feet off the flight controls, and remain ready to take control if required.

items.question: According to the level of attentiveness limitations (Sect. 2.6.2.1), how must the aircraft be flown below 10 ft AGL?
options: Hands-off is permitted if AP1 and AP2 are both engaged
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.2.1 states: above 500 ft AGL hands-off is permitted; below 500 ft attentive hands-off/on or manual; below 100 ft attentive hands-on or manual; below 10 ft AGL the aircraft shall be flown manually.

items.question: Below what height AGL is activation of the GA (go-around) mode prohibited?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.2.2 prohibits activation of the GA mode below 4 ft AGL.

items.question: What is the maximum forward airspeed for HOVER and SPEED HOLD mode, per Sect. 2.6.2.4?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.2.4 limits GTC, HOVER, or SPEED HOLD mode to the demonstrated wind conditions, with a max. forward airspeed of 50 kt for HOVER and SPEED HOLD mode, and requires visual flight only.

items.question: What is the minimum airspeed in instrument flight conditions (Vmini) with 4-axis AFCS on (3 upper modes engaged), versus otherwise?
options: 30 KIAS with 4-axis AFCS on; 60 KIAS otherwise
40 KIAS with 4-axis AFCS on; 60 KIAS otherwise
30 KIAS with 4-axis AFCS on; 50 KIAS otherwise
60 KIAS with 4-axis AFCS on; 30 KIAS otherwise
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.3.1 gives Vmini as 30 KIAS with 4-axis AFCS on (3 upper modes engaged), and 60 KIAS otherwise.

items.question: What is the maximum glideslope angle for an ILS approach versus an LPV/LNAV-VNAV approach, per Sect. 2.6.3.2?
options: 6.7° for ILS; 10.0° for LPV and LNAV/VNAV
10.0° for ILS; 6.7° for LPV and LNAV/VNAV
3.0° for ILS; 6.7° for LPV and LNAV/VNAV
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.3.2 gives a maximum glideslope angle of 6.7° for ILS approach, and 10.0° for LPV and LNAV/VNAV approach.

items.question: What is the maximum sustained rate of descent for an ILS/LOC/NDB/VOR/LPV/LNAV-VNAV approach, versus enroute?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.3.2 gives a maximum sustained rate of descent of 1000 ft/min for ILS, LOC, NDB, VOR, LPV or LNAV/VNAV approach, and 1500 ft/min enroute.

items.question: What is the maximum tailwind component permitted during steep approaches (>6°)?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.3.2 limits the maximum tailwind during steep approaches (>6°) to 15 kt.

items.question: In backup SAS mode or AFCS OFF, what is the maximum bank angle permitted?
options: 45° in backup SAS mode; 30° with AFCS OFF
30° in backup SAS mode; 45° with AFCS OFF
60° in backup SAS mode; 30° with AFCS OFF
There is no bank angle restriction in either mode
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.4.2 gives a maximum bank angle of 45° in backup SAS mode, and 30° with AFCS OFF (AP1, AP2 and BKUP all OFF). Maximum airspeed in either mode is 120 KIAS or Vne, whichever is less, and the aircraft must be flown manually.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.6.4.1, use of the DSAS mode (A.TRIM switched OFF) is limited to which situations, outside of the emergencies in Sect. 3?
options: Slope landings and training (with two pilots minimum for IMC training)
Any phase of flight without restriction
Only VMC training with a single pilot
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.4.1 limits DSAS mode use (outside of emergencies or MEL/MMEL provisions) to slope landings i.a.w. Sect. 4.10 and training; training in instrument flight conditions requires a minimum crew of two pilots, and the aircraft shall be flown manually in DSAS mode.

items.question: What restriction applies to sunglasses in the cockpit, per Sect. 2.7.1.6?
options: Sun glasses with polarized lenses shall not be used, as they could jeopardize readability of the GTN display
Sunglasses are prohibited entirely during IFR flight
There is no restriction on sunglasses
items.explanation: Sect. 2.7.1.6 states sun glasses with polarized lenses shall not be used, because this could jeopardize the readability of the GTN display.

items.question: What is the maximum approved gross mass, and the maximum approved ramp and taxi weight?
options: Max gross mass 2980 kg; max ramp/taxi weight 3000 kg
Max gross mass 3000 kg; max ramp/taxi weight 2980 kg
Max gross mass 2850 kg; max ramp/taxi weight 2980 kg
Max gross mass 2980 kg for both ramp/taxi and flight
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.1 gives the maximum approved ramp and taxi weight as 3000 kg, and the maximum approved gross mass as 2980 kg.

items.question: What is the minimum approved gross mass for flight?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.2 gives the minimum approved gross mass for flight as 1700 kg.

items.question: What is the maximum allowable load per tie-down ring, and per safety harness fitting (optional)?
options: 100 kg per tie-down ring; 230 kg per safety harness fitting
230 kg per tie-down ring; 100 kg per safety harness fitting
150 kg per tie-down ring; 150 kg per safety harness fitting
50 kg per tie-down ring; 100 kg per safety harness fitting
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.4 gives a maximum allowable load of 100 kg per tie-down ring, and Sect. 2.8.5 gives 230 kg per safety harness fitting.

items.question: If the VNE indication on the FND is not available, what airspeed shall be used for OEI operation under all conditions?
options: 110 kt, or as shown in the VNE tables, whichever is less
90 kt, or as shown in the VNE tables, whichever is less
150 kt fixed, as shown on the IESI
120 kt regardless of the VNE tables
items.explanation: Sect. 2.10.1 states that if the VNE indication on the FND is unavailable, VNE for OEI operation under all conditions is 110 kt, or as shown in the VNE tables (Table 2-1 to 2-3), whichever is less. For steady autorotation it is 90 kt.

items.question: What fixed VNE does the IESI (standby instrument) display, regardless of actual conditions?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.10.1 notes that the IESI instrument shows a fixed VNE of 150 kt; if the IESI has to be used as the reference instrument, the backup tables (Table 2-1 to 2-3) must be used to compute VNE.

items.question: What is the maximum operating altitude, and the maximum altitude for hover in ground effect, takeoff and landing?
options: Max operating altitude 20,000 ft; max HIGE/T.O/landing altitude 16,000 ft DA or PA, whichever is less
Max operating altitude 16,000 ft; max HIGE/T.O/landing altitude 20,000 ft
Max operating altitude 20,000 ft; max HIGE/T.O/landing altitude 20,000 ft
Max operating altitude 14,000 ft; max HIGE/T.O/landing altitude 12,000 ft
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.1 gives the maximum operating altitude as 20,000 ft, and the maximum altitude for hover in ground effect, takeoff and landing as 16,000 ft DA or PA, whichever is less.

items.question: What is the maximum and minimum ambient air temperature, per Sect. 2.11.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.2 gives maximum air temperature as ISA+39°C (max. +50°C), and minimum air temperature as -35°C. If OAT ≥40°C, maximum ground operating time is limited to 30 minutes.

items.question: If OAT is 40°C or above, what is the maximum permitted operating time on the ground?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.2 states that if OAT ≥40°C, the maximum operating time on ground is limited to 30 minutes.

items.question: What is the minimum battery temperature if the aircraft battery is used for engine starting?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.4 states the minimum battery temperature (if battery is used for engine starting) is -20°C; for start-up at OAT below -20°C using the aircraft battery, the battery shall be preheated to at least -20°C.

items.question: Main rotor lead-lag resonance may occur in which rotor RPM range, and what action does the WARNING require?
options: 60-68% rotor RPM — maintain cyclic neutral and collective full down
80-90% rotor RPM — maintain cyclic neutral and collective full down
50-60% rotor RPM — apply full collective immediately
97-105% rotor RPM — no specific action required
items.explanation: Sect. 2.12 WARNING states main rotor lead-lag resonance may occur in the 60-68% rotor RPM range; any stimulation of lead-lag oscillation in this range may severely damage the main rotor blades, so the cyclic stick must be kept neutral and the collective full down.

items.question: The takeoff power (TOP) rating on the FLI is limited to how long, per Sect. 2.13.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.1 states the amber rectangle on the FLI (takeoff power rating) use is limited to maximum 5 minutes, with a white countdown displayed 90 seconds before expiry and an audio tone 15 seconds before expiry.

items.question: What is the OEI 30 second power torque limit, and how must its use be recorded?
options: 128% (1 engine); use and duration must be recorded in the aircraft logbook
89.5% (1 engine); use must be reported to maintenance only if exceeded
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.2 gives the OEI 30 sec power torque limit as 128% (single engine), and requires use and duration of the OEI 30 sec rating to be recorded in the aircraft logbook.

items.question: What is the AEO max continuous torque limit, per Sect. 2.13.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.2 gives AEO max continuous torque as 2 x 69% (both engines), takeoff power (5 min) as 2 x 78% below Vy+5kt, and transient (unintended, max 10 sec) as 2 x 82% below Vy+5kt.

items.question: What is the OEI 30 second power TOT limit, per Sect. 2.13.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.3 gives OEI TOT limits: max continuous 942°C, 2 min power 994°C, 30 sec power 1024°C.

items.question: What is the starting transient TOT limit (max. 5 sec), per Sect. 2.13.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.3 gives continuous starting TOT limit as 819°C, and starting transient (max. 5 sec) as 910°C.

items.question: What is the engine oil pressure range for continuous operation, and the maximum for engine starting (max. 2 min.)?
options: 1.3-5 bar continuous; 10-15 bar for starting (max 2 min)
1.3-10 bar continuous; 15 bar fixed for starting
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.1 gives continuous operation engine oil pressure as 1.3-5 bar, caution range 5-10 bar, maximum 10 bar, and for engine starting (max. 2 min.) 10-15 bar.

items.question: What is the starter energize duty cycle if a 25 Ah, 26 Ah, or 27 Ah battery is installed?
options: 30 s ON, 60 s OFF — 30 s ON, 60 s OFF — 30 s ON, 30 min OFF
15 s ON, 30 s OFF — 15 s ON, 30 s OFF — 15 s ON, 30 min OFF
45 s ON, 15 s OFF, repeated indefinitely
60 s ON, 30 s OFF, no cooldown required
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.3 gives, for 25/26/27 Ah battery installations: 30 s ON, 60 s OFF, repeated, then 30 s ON followed by a 30 minute cooling period. The 15 s ON/30 s OFF cycle applies instead when a 40 Ah or 44 Ah battery is installed or a ground power unit is used.

items.question: What is the maximum continuous generator load per generator below 15,000 ft PA, versus above?
options: 200 A below 15,000 ft; 180 A above 15,000 ft
180 A below 15,000 ft; 200 A above 15,000 ft
250 A below 15,000 ft; 200 A above 15,000 ft
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.3.1 gives maximum continuous generator load as 200 A for PA below 15,000 ft, and 180 A for PA above 15,000 ft.

items.question: What is the maximum current flow permitted when using a 28V DC ground power unit for starting?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.4 limits current flow to 700 A maximum when using 28V DC ground power units for starting, and cautions that the EPU must only be connected if the battery is connected.

items.question: What is the main transmission oil temperature range for continuous operation, and the absolute maximum?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.6 gives main transmission oil temperature: caution range -45°C to 0°C, continuous operation 0°C to 105°C, caution range 105°C to 120°C, maximum 120°C.

items.question: On the mast moment indicator, what percentage range is amber, and at what percentage does red begin?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.7.1 gives the mast moment ranges: normal 0% to 49.9%, amber 50% to 66%, red above 66%, with white marking the end of scale at 100%. A voice message "MAST MOMENT" triggers when the red limit is exceeded.

items.question: What is the maximum fuel viscosity permitted, per Sect. 2.15.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.15.1 gives the maximum fuel viscosity as 12 cSt.

items.question: Which Chinese fuel additives are explicitly noted as NOT approved for use, per Sect. 2.15.5?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.15.5 explicitly notes that Chinese additives T1502, T1601 and T1602 are not approved for use, while EGME and DiEGME type anti-icing additives are the approved types.

items.question: What is the required concentration by volume for anti-icing fuel additives, per Sect. 2.15.5.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.15.5.1 requires anti-icing additive concentration by volume of max 0.15%, min 0.10%.

items.question: What is the total usable fuel quantity for the H135 T3 (main + supply tanks combined)?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.15.6 gives total usable fuel (main + 2x supply tanks) as 700.55 litres / 560.40 kg, out of a total fuel capacity of 710.0 litres / 568.00 kg (unusable fuel: 9.45 litres / 7.6 kg).

items.question: What is the primary source for fuel quantity information, per the CAUTION in Sect. 2.15.6?
options: The displayed digital value; the pictorial indication must be confirmed by the digital value
Either indication may be used interchangeably
items.explanation: The CAUTION in Sect. 2.15.6 states the primary source for fuel quantity information is the displayed digital value; the pictorial indication has to be confirmed by the digital value.

items.question: What is the main transmission oil quantity range, per Sect. 2.16.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.16.2 gives oil quantities: engines 4.85 litres each, main transmission 10.0-12.0 litres, fenestron gearbox 0.5 litres.

items.question: What are the hydraulic system fluid quantities for hydraulic system 1 and system 2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.17.2 gives hydraulic system quantities: system 1 = 1.0 litres, system 2 = 1.2 litres, using MIL-PRF-5606 fluid.

items.question: According to the mass and gross mass placard referenced in Sect. 2.18, what maximum permissible gross mass is shown?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.18 describes the placard below the forward RH cabin door reading "MAX. PERMISS. GROSS MASS 2980 kg", matching the maximum approved gross mass given in Sect. 2.8.1.
